Last month, after the TV tracking app TV Time officially shut down, one of its co-founders, Antonio Pinto, immediately announced the launch of a brand-new film and TV tracking app called Bingers, which places a greater emphasis on social features. Here is a detailed introduction.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media previously announced the closure of its film and TV tracking app TV Time, and one of the co-founders immediately unveiled Bingers, positioned as "a fast and beautiful watchlist combined with a fun community."

According to TechCrunch, Bingers is now available for download on iOS and Android platforms, offering users still searching for an alternative to TV Time a sort of spiritual successor. TV Time was once one of the most popular film and TV tracking apps globally.

Users who previously used TV Time and saved their data through the platform's export tool before shutdown can import their archived records into Bingers for a seamless transition, while users who never exported their data, or newcomers encountering a film and TV tracking app for the first time, can start from scratch.

Bingers strongly emphasizes community-driven features, such as profiles, comments, show ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity elections. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features were the key to TV Time's enduring appeal:

If users simply want a straightforward platform to record the TV shows and movies they have watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlist and viewing history features. Similar to TV Time, it also displays a calendar of upcoming or premiering shows, indicating how many days remain until release.

Bingers is available for free download on the App Store, with no in-app purchases currently offered.
